question: Is there a periodic parent tiling, with labels, all of whose labelled collars lie among the labelled parent collars surviving LAST-BIT-20261108-001B for s = 10101 / 00110, one of them off-law, with a period found near the seed and at most 48 tiles per period? Its cut would be a periodic plane obeying the decoration's law that is not a pinwheel tiling: a crystal escaping the last one-bit decoration.

public_inputs.law: S1*, as in E001: the 513 labelled parent collars surviving LAST-BIT-20261108-001B (310 in L(s), 50 pinwheel collars with labels L(s) does not list, 153 non-pinwheel collars), both handednesses.
public_inputs.candidate periods: E001's: for each seed, two patches grown by exhaustive extension to tile distance 2 (move orders shuffled by seeds 0 and 1, 3,000 steps each); translation vectors between two of their tiles with the same shape and label and Euclidean length at most 9 (the seed's short leg is 1), and between complete tiles with the same labelled collar.
public_inputs.filters: Two exact necessary conditions on a crystal containing the seed collar C: (1) its tiles per period are at least n(C), the number of distinct (shape, label) classes among C's tiles, since tiles of one orbit share both; (2) every period v is compatible with C: each tile of C + v and of C - v is a tile of C with the same label or overlaps none of C's tiles. Candidate periods are filtered by (2), and so is every vector of each lattice up to the collar's Euclidean diameter (longer translates meet no tile of C).
public_inputs.lattices: The lattices spanned by two compatible periods with n(C) to 48 tiles per period, every vector up to the collar's diameter compatible with C, ordered by tiles per period and then basis length; at most 200 per seed.
public_inputs.torus growth: E001's torus_lib.torus_grow, unchanged: growth on the lattice's torus from the seed collar, depth first with backtracking, 1,000 steps.
public_inputs.check: E001's: every completed torus as a ROUND-PRICE-20261108-001A decor_lib plane, every cell collar a core collar, and its cut admitting a periodic labelling obeying L(s) on the plane's own lattice.

forbidden_inputs: Changing the law, the seeds, the candidate periods, the filters, the lattice bound, the budgets or the check after seeing results
Dropping seeds or lattices that complete a torus
primary_observable: Whether some seed completes a torus that passes the check, with its tiles per period.
secondary_observables: Per seed: n(C), candidate and compatible periods, lattices spanned and lattices kept, and torus outcomes; the number of seeds with any compatible period and with any kept lattice.
cheapest_meaningful_control: Positive: E001's. For the constant decoration with the law Q(L) of its labelled level-one collars, the rhombus lattice's collar as seed must pass both filters with the rhombus lattice and complete a torus that passes the check under that decoration's law. A run whose control fails is not read.
decision_or_followup_rule: If a seed completes a torus that passes the check, the decoration fails: one bit per tile, as a decorated substitution, fails in all 1,024 cases. If none does, the attempt is negative within its candidate periods and budgets; the one-bit line is paused with the case recorded open, as the coordinator planned.
stop_rule: Stop at the declared seeds, patches, candidate periods, filters, lattices and budgets.
nonclaims: Exploratory and non-promotable: candidate periods come from two patches per seed, not from an exhaustive list, and each torus search is exhaustive only within its budget.
No crystal found does not show that the decoration forces the pinwheel; a non-periodic plane could escape it as well.
feasibility_disclosure: Frozen after E001 was stopped (its interpretation.md): E001's 1,440 attempts on 12 seeds were all invalid. Before freezing, the steps with filter (2) on spanning periods only were run on the control (69 of 87 periods compatible; 200 lattices of 4 to 18 tiles; 16 tori, the rhombus lattice and its multiples, 4 to 16 tiles) and on three seeds (41 to 46 of 62 to 76 periods compatible, the shortest of length 5; all 200 lattices invalid, on one seed checked because the seed collar overlapped a translate by a short lattice vector, which led to filtering every lattice vector up to the collar's diameter).
